items.title: Reversal of Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI-Assessed Left Atrial Fibrosis Following Cardioversion in Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
items.abstract: Previous studies have shown that atrial fibrillation (AF) cardioversion may reverse atrial remodeling. To investigate whether LGE-MRI-assessed left atrial (LA) fibrosis regresses after persistent atrial fibrillation (PersAF) cardioversion to sinus rhythm, and to analyze the relationship between fibrosis change and traditional volume-based measures of LA reverse remodeling. Prospective. Fifty-three patients following cardioversion for PersAF. 3 T, cine balanced steady-state free precession cine and 3D inversion recovery gradient-echo sequences. MRI was performed 1-3 days after AF-cardioversion (early follow-up), and again at 3 months (late follow-up). Image analysis was performed by two observers using CVI42 and ADAS software. Data were compared between early and late follow-up. LA fibrosis on LGE-MRI was categorized by the image intensity ratio (IIR): core zone (IIR > 1.61) and border zone (0.97 < IIR ≤ 1.61). Maximum LA volume (LAVmax), LA ejection fraction (LAEF), LA strain, and left ventricular mass were assessed from cine data. An LAVmax reduction ≥ 15% from early to late follow-up defined LA reverse remodeling. Early and late follow-up data were compared using paired t-tests. Multivariable analysis was performed to assess the associations between changes in LA border and core zone and other LA parameters. A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant. Seventeen patients had volume-based LA reverse. Compared with early follow-up, LA border zone (22.2 [11.8-37.0] vs. 18.1 [11.8-25.2] cm 2 ) and core zone (0.9 ± 3.0 vs. 0.1 ± 0.6 cm 2 ) were significantly decreased. LAV max was significantly reduced (97.2 ± 26.3 vs. 109.4 ± 32.7 mL), and LAEF (44.1 ± 15.8 vs. 32.2% ± 13.1%) and LA strain (27.4 ± 14.1 vs. 18.2% ± 8.6%) improved. Volume-based LA reverse remodeling was unrelated to ΔLA border (p = 0.955) or Δcore zone (p = 0.301). PersAF conversion to sinus rhythm resulted in a reduction in LGE-defined atrial enhancement, LAV reduction, and improved function. Fibrosis regression was independent of volume-based LA reverse remodeling. 2. Stage 4. This study used cardiac MRI to examine left atrial changes after cardioversion for persistent atrial fibrillation. In 53 patients, atrial scar‐like enhancement decreased 3 months after restoring normal heart rhythm, alongside smaller atrial volume and better atrial function. Such reduction in enhancement was not linked to volume‐based atrial reverse remodeling.

items.title: Family Resilience and Dyadic Health Outcomes in Heart Failure: An Integrative Review of Pathways and Underlying Mechanisms.
items.abstract: Heart failure (HF) affects more than 64 million people worldwide and places substantial physical, emotional, and financial burdens on patients and family caregivers. Although family resilience is a crucial protective factor in chronic illness, evidence concerning its role in HF dyads remains fragmented because quantitative and qualitative findings have not been sufficiently integrated across populations and study designs. This integrative review synthesized evidence on family resilience in HF patient-caregiver dyads, examined its mechanisms and asymmetric effects, and identified implications for practice and research. A systematic search of 13 databases was conducted from inception to February 15, 2026. Of 677 records identified, 34 studies met the inclusion criteria. Design-appropriate tools were used for quality appraisal, and thematic synthesis was guided by the Walsh Family Resilience Framework. Family resilience operated through three core dimensions: belief systems, organizational patterns, and communication processes. Its protective effects were mediated by mutuality, resilience, and self-efficacy and moderated by factors including disease stage and gender. Dyadic care and management patterns ranged from patient-oriented and caregiver-oriented approaches to collaborative and complementary approaches. Four intervention strategies were identified: assessment and stratification, dyadic interaction and caregiver empowerment, multi-target integration, and strengths-based care. These findings support the development of family-centered care programs to improve continuity of care, quality of life, and health outcomes in HF dyads. Longitudinal studies and randomized clinical trials are needed to further examine the dynamic nature of family resilience.

items.title: Optical Coherence Tomography can identify Non-Ischemic Lesions that have a Benign Outcome from those with High-Risk of Future Events. Insights from a Patient Level Pooled Analysis of COMBINE (OCT-FFR) and PECTUS-Obs Prospective Natural History Studies.
items.abstract: Whether all lipid-rich plaques (LRP) or only thin-cap fibroatheromas (TCFA) are at risk for future events, remains unclear. Individual patient data from two prospective studies, the COMBINE FFR-OCT and PECTUS-obs trials, performed respectively in a diabetes mellitus (DM) and myocardial infraction, (MI) patients, were pooled. Patients carrying ≥1 fractional-flow reserve (FFR) negative, optical coherence tomography (OCT) -assessed, lesions (target lesions) were divided in two groups. The first group represented patients with non-LRP and the second those with LRP. The second group was further divided in LRP-TCFAs and LRP thick-cap fibroatheromas (ThCFAs). Patients with plaque rupture or erosion were further excluded from the Non-LPR and ThCFA groups. The primary endpoint was target-lesion failure, defined as cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction and target-lesion revascularization at 2 years. Pooling of the two trials resulted in 722 patients carrying non-destabilized, ≥1 FFR-negative, OCT assessed lesions, of which 165 (22.8%) had non-LRP while 557 (77.2%) had LRP. In the LPR group, 224 patients (40.2%) had TCFA morphology. The primary endpoint was 29(5.2%) vs 4(2.4%) (HR 2.21, CI: (0.78-6.28), p= 0.14) in the LRP versus non-LRP groups. However, within LRP groups TCFAs were associated with a significantly higher primary endpoint rate than ThCFAs; 20 (8.9%) vs 9 (2.7%), (HR 3.22, CI: 1.46-7,11, p < 0.01). At 2 years only TCFAs were associated with a high rate of TLF while the remaining non-ischemic LRP and non-LRP plaques had a very benign outcome under optimal statin-based medical treatment.

Surgical decompression of uveal melanoma with optic chiasmal extension via a modified orbitozygomatic approach: illustrative case.
items.abstract: Uveal melanoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy of adulthood. Perineural spread along the optic nerve to the optic chiasm is exceedingly rare, with only 4 previously published cases. No standard neurosurgical management has been established. A 65-year-old woman presented with progressive right-sided monocular vision loss over 1 year, subsequently developing left temporal hemianopia. MRI demonstrated a 3.3 × 2.9 × 2.2-cm right intraconal mass extending through the orbital apex along the optic nerve to the optic chiasm, with a 2.8 × 1.9 × 1.5-cm suprasellar component. A right modified one-piece orbitozygomatic craniotomy achieved subtotal resection of the suprasellar disease and decompressed the contralateral optic nerve. The patient received combination ipilimumab/nivolumab, 60 Gy in 30 fractions adjuvant orbital radiotherapy, nivolumab/relatlimab (progression), 27 Gy in 3 fractions stereotactic radiosurgery for new intracranial metastases, and salvage temozolomide with bevacizumab. She remained alive with stable disease at 12 months. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first reported case of uveal melanoma with optic chiasmal extension managed by a modified orbitozygomatic approach. Contralateral visual field deficits in a patient with an ipsilateral orbital mass should prompt dedicated cranial imaging. Multidisciplinary care can achieve meaningful disease control even when first-line immunotherapies fail. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26734.

items.title: Multicenter Randomized Phase II Trial of Maintenance Systemic Therapy Versus Local Consolidative Therapy Plus Maintenance Systemic Therapy for Limited Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NRG-LU002).
items.abstract: First-line treatments for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable mutations include immunotherapy (IO) and/or chemotherapy. The NRG-LU002 randomized phase II trial evaluated the addition of local consolidative therapy (LCT)-radiation and/or surgery-to maintenance systemic therapy (MST) in oligometastatic NSCLC. Patients with metastatic NSCLC and up to three residual extracranial metastatic sites (excluding primary) showing stable disease or partial response after four courses of first-line therapy were randomly assigned 1:2 to MST alone or LCT followed by MST. LCT permitted included stereotactic body radiation therapy, hypofractionated radiation, and/or surgery. Stratification was by histology and IO use. The primary end point was progression-free survival (PFS), with secondary end points including overall survival (OS), quality of life, and toxicity. From April 2017 to November 2021, 215 patients (81 MST and 134 LCT + MST) enrolled at 68 sites (median age 65 years, 78% nonsquamous histology, 90% IO-based therapy). Median follow-up was 21.9 months. PFS rates at 1 and 2 years, respectively, were 48.0% and 35.9% (MST) versus 51.5% and 40.1% (LCT + MST), with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.93 ( P = .66). Among IO-treated patients, PFS HR was 0.90. OS HRs were 1.05 for both all patients and IO subgroup. Grade ≥2 adverse events were more frequent in LCT + MST (84% v 73%, P = .05), including grade ≥3 pneumonitis (10% v 1%, P = .02). Early pneumonitis was linked to worse PFS/OS. Longer MST (>6 months) correlated with improved outcomes by landmark analyses. Liver metastases and poor performance status predicted worse prognosis. Adding LCT to IO-based first-line therapy in oligometastatic NSCLC did not improve PFS or OS. Increased toxicity from local treatment reduced MST administration, affecting outcomes. Further refinement of patient selection is needed to optimize LCT therapeutic ratios.

items.title: Protein spherical nucleic acids enable multivalent display of TLR9 agonists for enhanced cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Precise control over nanoparticle composition and molecular architecture remains a fundamental challenge in nanomedicine, limiting systematic exploration of therapeutic design and biological function. Here, we report structurally defined protein spherical nucleic acids (ProSNAs) comprising ferritin nanocages densely functionalized with Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) agonist, immunostimulatory oligonucleotide shell for cancer immunotherapy. ProSNAs are rapidly internalized by immune cells, elicit potent innate immune activation, and exhibit prolonged intratumoral retention with preferential uptake by myeloid cells. These responses promote dendritic cell maturation, polarize macrophages toward an antitumor phenotype, and stimulate robust CD8 + T cell-mediated immunity. Across murine melanoma, colon adenocarcinoma, and triple-negative breast cancer models, a single intratumoral administration of ProSNAs induces durable tumor regression, suppresses metastatic progression, and synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade. Taken together, these findings establish ProSNAs as a structurally defined, myeloid-targeting nanomedicine platform for programmable cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Tumor cell-intrinsic E47 functions as a critical suppressor in antitumor immunity via the FBXL2-PD-L1 axis.
items.abstract: The transcription factor E47, encoded by the TCF3 gene, is essential for B and T cell lineage commitment and development. However, whether tumor cell-intrinsic E47 contributes to tumor immunosurveillance remains unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that E47 functions as a critical suppressor of antitumor immunity. Clinical analyses reveal that increased intratumoral TCF3 expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Silencing of E47 in tumor cells markedly inhibits tumor growth, increases infiltration of cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, and decreases PD-L1 expression. Mechanistically, E47 transcriptionally represses FBXL2 , which encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes PD-L1 polyubiquitination at K270 and proteasomal degradation. Restoration of FBXL2 effectively reverses E47-induced PD-L1 upregulation and tumor growth. Strikingly, Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug nebivolol, an activator of FBXL2, significantly enhances antitumor immunity and improves the efficacy of CTLA-4 blockade therapy in syngeneic tumor mouse models. Together, this study uncovers the E47-FBXL2 axis as a critical pathway governing PD-L1 stability and antitumor immunity, highlighting its therapeutic potential for improving the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: People living with HIV have increased CD4+ T cell metabolic activity and reduced influenza-reactive cellular responses to vaccination.
items.abstract: While antiretroviral therapy has improved health outcomes for people living with HIV (PLWH), individuals still experience chronic immune activation and increased incidence of comorbidities. This study investigated basal immunometabolic function and influenza vaccine-induced antibody and T cell responses in 13 PLWH on antiretroviral therapy with suppressed virus and 17 individuals living without HIV (PLWoH). We found similar serum hemagglutination inhibition antibody titers against influenza A (H1N1, H3N2) or influenza B (B-Victoria, B-Yamagata) antigens between PLWH and PLWoH pre- and postvaccination. While PLWH had higher baseline frequencies of influenza-reactive CD4+ T cells expressing OX40 and CD40L compared with PLWoH, only PLWoH had significantly increased frequencies of influenza-reactive CD4+ T cells in response to influenza vaccination. Naive and memory CD4+ T cells from PLWH exhibited higher basal metabolic activity with increased metabolic dysfunction compared with PLWoH. These findings suggest that while PLWH can mount humoral responses to influenza vaccination, increased CD4+ T cell activation and altered CD4+ T cell metabolism may influence cellular immune responses to vaccination. This highlights how the adaptive immune system in PLWH is affected even when HIV replication is controlled through ART.

items.title: Immunogenicity of titer guided intensified hepatitis B vaccination strategy in children with cancer.
items.abstract: To assess the immunogenicity of a titer-guided, intensified hepatitis B vaccination protocol in children with malignancies receiving chemotherapy. This retrospective cohort study included children aged   100 mIU/mL received no additional vaccination. Follow-up anti-HBs titers were assessed to evaluate immune response. Among 169 children, follow-up anti-HBs titers were available for 135. At baseline, 79 (46.7%) children had anti-HBs   100 mIU/mL. Among 94 vaccinated children, 47 (50.0%) achieved a robust serological response (> 100 mIU/mL). Robust responses were more frequent in those with baseline anti-HBs titers of 10-100 mIU/mL. Response rates were higher in younger children, but the difference was not statistically significant. A titer-guided intensified hepatitis B vaccination strategy was associated with robust serological response, particularly in children with partial pre-existing immunity.

items.title: Expanding the Clinical Nurse Specialist Role Beyond Traditional Settings: A CNS-Led Independent Practice Model.
items.abstract: The clinical nurse specialist (CNS) role has historically been associated with inpatient leadership, quality improvement, staff mentorship, and systems-level practice within hospital environments. Although CNS education prepares advanced practice registered nurses to function across direct patient care, nursing practice, and organizational leadership spheres, limited literature exists describing CNS-led outpatient or independent practice models. This article describes the development and implementation of a CNS-led nonprofit hybrid telehealth practice established in Michigan in 2025 that provides psychiatric medication management, addiction medicine, harm reduction services, hepatitis C treatment, HIV prevention, sexually transmitted infection care, and limited primary care services for adult populations. The practice demonstrates how CNS competencies may extend beyond traditional inpatient environments to address health care access gaps through innovative community-based care delivery. Operational elements, including payer credentialing, electronic medical record implementation, workflow development, nonprofit formation, interdisciplinary referral partnerships, and hybrid telehealth infrastructure, are discussed through the lens of CNS systems leadership competencies. This article highlights the potential for CNS-led outpatient practice models to expand health care access, strengthen continuity of care, and support population health initiatives while advocating for broader recognition of the CNS role outside traditional health care systems.

items.title: Integrated Methods for Survey Outreach in an Assessment of Chemical Exposures Investigation After a Train Derailment-East Palestine, Ohio, 2023.
items.abstract: An Assessment of Chemical Exposures (ACE) is a rapid investigation method used by public health agencies to evaluate potential exposures and health effects after environmental incidents. After a train derailment and subsequent release of hazardous substances in East Palestine, Ohio, and surrounding areas, multiple approaches supported survey outreach among affected communities during an ACE investigation and are described in this report. An incident-specific, cross-sectional ACE survey tool was developed for administration through in-person interviews at a temporary health center, online self-administration, and door-to-door surveys. Geospatial mapping of respondent addresses aimed to inform additional survey outreach efforts. In addition to serving as a centralized site for survey administration, the temporary health center also provided on-site mental health support, referrals for healthcare, and additional resources, including contacts for home air or water quality testing, and basic supplies such as bottled water and food vouchers. ACE surveys were administered by nurses at a temporary health center located within a church in East Palestine, Ohio. Iterative geospatial mapping of respondent addresses identified areas with low survey response rates, informing targeted door-to-door survey efforts to increase participation in affected communities. Door-to-door survey administration by public health professionals was supported by collaboration with local fire departments. A total of 527 participants completed surveys in Ohio; 335 (64%) were completed at the health center, 146 (27%) online, and 46 (9%) during door-to-door efforts. Geospatial mapping and subsequent door-to-door survey administration improved neighborhood response rates from 0.5% to 24% in the target neighborhood with the lowest survey coverage. The use of a temporary health center for centralized survey administration, geospatial mapping to guide additional survey outreach, and strategic collaborations with local community partners facilitated the completion of the ACE survey for the rapid evaluation of health symptoms and resource needs postincident.

items.title: Evaluation of the surveillance-based 'Data-to-Suppression' intervention in a cluster-randomized, stepped-wedge trial in Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program Part A service settings.
items.abstract: To enhance Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program (RWHAP)-funded service providers' resources to address unsuppressed HIV viral load (VL), we implemented a Data-to-Suppression (D2S) intervention, including semi-annual surveillance-based reports listing each service site's virally unsuppressed RWHAP clients and capacity-building assistance for follow-up activities. In two stages one year apart, we implemented D2S with 27 RWHAP housing and/or behavioral-health service sites. Analyses included clients listed on sites' D2S reports and verified as living and unsuppressed at time of report issue. Randomizing sites within matched pairs to early or delayed intervention starts, we evaluated D2S effectiveness through a stepped-wedge trial. We assessed timely viral suppression (TVS: any VL <200 copies/mL ≤6 months following D2S report inclusion) and time to viral suppression (months between report inclusion and first VL <200 copies/mL within 12 months). Reports were generated for three periods: Period 0 (no D2S), Period 1 (D2S at sites assigned to early implementation), and Period 2 (D2S at all sites), but released to sites only when they were assigned to implement D2S. Of 1,494 opportunities for TVS (among 1,077 clients), 44.2% (95% CI: 41.7%, 46.8%) yielded TVS. The conditional maximum likelihood estimate for the odds ratio (TVS versus no TVS comparing D2S to usual practice) was 0.97 (95% CI: 0.58, 1.63). The hazards ratio for time to viral suppression in D2S versus usual practice was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.51, 1.17). Our point estimates for D2S effects were nonsignificant; the confidence intervals preclude definitive conclusions about intervention effectiveness.

items.title: Targeting PI3K signalling for broad inhibition of β-Coronavirus infection.
items.abstract: The phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) signalling pathway plays a central role in regulating key cellular processes such as survival, metabolism, and immune responses. Aberrant activation of this pathway is associated with tumorigenesis, and several PI3K inhibitors have been developed as anticancer agents. Emerging evidence suggests that viruses, including β-coronaviruses, have evolved mechanisms to exploit host PI3K signalling for their replication and immune evasion. In this study, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of a panel of PI3K inhibitors against β-coronaviruses, including murine hepatitis virus (MHV), human OC43 (HuCoV-OC43) and four major SARS-CoV-2 variants using both cell line and organoid models. Our findings reveal that these compounds exhibit low micromolar potency in inhibiting viral replication. Notably, the PI3K/mTOR inhibitor C20 (PWT33597) demonstrated broad-spectrum activity against multiple β-coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, MHV, and HuCoV-OC43, in conventional cell lines and in air-liquid interface (ALI)-cultured, differentiated primary human bronchial epithelial cells. Given that cytokine storm is a major contributor to SARS-CoV-2-related multi-organ failure and mortality, we further explored the impact of PI3K inhibition on host inflammatory responses. We found that MHV infection markedly increased cytokine expression in RAW264.7 macrophages. Interestingly, treatment with C20 further amplified cytokine production, suggesting complex immunomodulatory effects that may not be universally beneficial. Together, our findings indicate that PI3K inhibitors such as C20 exhibit promising broad-spectrum antiviral activity. Although their immunomodulatory effects, such as enhanced cytokine production, warrant further investigation, these compounds may offer a dual opportunity to fine-tune both antiviral and host immune responses with appropriate therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Development of the decisional balance scale for health behaviors after transarterial chemoembolization in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A Modified Delphi Study.
items.abstract: Based on the decisional balance construct within the Transtheoretical Model, a preliminary instrument for evaluating health behavior decision-making among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma following transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) was developed. The Delphi expert consultation method was then used to assess item appropriateness, the degree of expert consensus, and content validity. This process provides an empirical foundation for subsequent refinement of the scale and its further psychometric validation in clinical practice. A modified Delphi method was employed. Between 10/12/2025 and 27/01/2026, 24 experts specializing in liver cancer patient care, interventional nursing, and psychological nursing from 16 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities) across China were invited to rate the importance and feasibility of each item. The response rates for both rounds of expert consultation were 100%. The expert authority coefficients (Cr) were 0.92 and 0.94 for rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Kendall's coefficients of concordance (W) for importance ratings were 0.363 and 0.385, respectively; for feasibility ratings, they were 0.253 and 0.358, respectively. All differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05). The preliminary version of the final scale comprises two dimensions, namely, perceived benefits (pros) and perceived barriers (cons), covering physical activity, medication adherence, nutritional management, and follow-up care. This study developed a preliminary health behavior decisional balance scale for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma following TACE. Through Delphi expert consultation, a consensus was achieved, and acceptable content validity was established. The scale provides a preliminary tool for assessing patients' health behavior decision-making tendencies and for identifying perceived benefits and barriers to adoption of behavior. Further psychometric evaluation in clinical samples is needed to verify the reliability and validity of the scale, as well as its potential for clinical application.

items.title: Spatial profiling of primary CRC and synchronous lung and liver metastases identifies a liver-specific stromal niche associated with immune exclusion.
items.abstract: Liver metastases from microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC) demonstrate profound resistance to immune checkpoint therapy (ICT) compared with extrahepatic disease, but the tissue-specific mechanisms remain unclear. We sought to determine how organ-specific microenvironments shape immune exclusion in MSS CRC metastases. We performed spatial transcriptomic profiling and multiplex immunofluorescence on synchronous liver and lung metastases, along with matched primary CRC tumors, from patients with MSS CRC. Spatially resolved regions of tumor core and invasive margin were analyzed for immune and stromal composition. Clinical relevance was assessed using survival analyses in the TCGA-COAD/READ cohort. Liver metastases exhibited a dense, fibrotic microenvironment enriched with activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), MRC1+/SPP1+ immunosuppressive macrophages, and elevated CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling. Spatial analyses revealed stromal-associated effector T-cell exclusion from the tumor core in liver metastases, with T cells restricted to the invasive margin. Conversely, synchronous lung metastases showed sparse stroma and uniform infiltration of proliferating B and T cells. Coordinated enrichment of aHSCs and macrophages defined a liver-specific stromal-myeloid niche associated with immune exclusion. High aHSC gene signature expression correlated with significantly worse progression-free survival in the TCGA cohort. These findings identify liver-specific stromal programming, associated with aHSCs and CXCL12-CXCR4 signaling, as a candidate contributor of immune exclusion in MSS CRC. Targeting liver-specific stromal-immune interactions may represent a therapeutic strategy to enhance ICT efficacy in liver-dominant metastatic CRC.
items.journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research

items.title: Diseases causing nervous signs in cattle in South America.
items.abstract: Neurological diseases in cattle are among the most important diagnostic challenges in veterinary practice and diagnostic laboratories. In South America, surveillance systems and diagnostic networks have progressively expanded the recognition of diseases causing nervous signs in cattle, yet available information remains fragmented across countries. This review integrates current knowledge on the main diseases causing nervous signs in cattle in South America, with emphasis on their clinical presentation, etiopathogenesis, pathology, and diagnostic relevance, and includes brief information on treatment, control, and prevention. For practical purposes, bovine neurologic disorders are organized according to their etiologic origin into infectious, parasitic, toxic, metabolic, neoplastic, and genetic or congenital. Among infectious conditions, rabies remains the most important viral encephalitis in the region, while bovine herpesviral meningoencephalitis, malignant catarrhal fever, listeriosis, thrombotic meningoencephalitis, and suppurative bacterial infections are also relevant differential diagnoses. Parasitic disorders such as cerebral babesiosis, Trypanosoma vivax infection, nervous coccidiosis, neosporosis, coenurosis, and amoebic meningoencephalitis are less frequent but regionally significant. Toxic and metabolic causes are highly diverse and include plant and fungal intoxications, pesticide and lead poisoning, polioencephalomalacia, hypomagnesemia, vitamin A deficiency, ketosis/fatty liver syndrome, and hypocalcemia. Less common but clinically important conditions include nervous system neoplasms and congenital or hereditary disorders. A single integrated table summarizes, for each condition, the etiologic agent, geographic distribution, affected age group and neurolocalization, main neurological syndrome, principal lesions, field diagnostic aids, samples for laboratory confirmation, laboratory diagnostic methods, and the available treatment and control measures. This review highlights the wide etiologic spectrum of bovine diseases causing nervous signs in South America and emphasizes the importance of a systematic diagnostic approach integrating epidemiology, clinical neurology, gross pathology, histopathology, and targeted ancillary tests. A better understanding of these conditions should improve differential diagnosis, therapeutic decision-making, surveillance, and preventive strategies in cattle production systems across the region.

items.title: Diffusion MRI and Inflammation-Nutrition-Based Nomogram for Early Tumor Response to HAIC-Based Triple Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma with Portal Vein Tumor Thrombus.
items.abstract: To develop and evaluate a pretreatment nomogram predicting early objective response to HAIC-based triple therapy in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus. This retrospective three-center study included 170 patients (training, 82; pooled external validation, 88). The nomogram incorporated ln(SII), prognostic nutritional index, and normalized diffusion-weighted imaging-to-apparent diffusion coefficient ratio. Evaluation included discrimination, calibration, decision curves, 500-bootstrap internal validation, SHAP interpretation, and survival stratification. Objective response occurred in 27/82 (32.9%) training patients and 30/88 (34.1%) external patients. The areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879-0.989) and 0.924 (95% CI, 0.869-0.978); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.917. At the training-derived probability cutoff of 0.1933, sensitivity was 92.6% (95% CI, 76.6-97.9%) and 90.0% (95% CI, 74.4-96.5%), respectively. External calibration showed a Brier score of 0.112 and a slope of 1.456. The model had higher AUCs than Child-Pugh class, ALBI grade, and the six-and-twelve category. Higher predicted response probability was associated with longer overall and progression-free survival in both cohorts (all log-rank p  < 0.001). The nomogram showed promising discrimination for early objective response in selected patients with HCC and PVTT receiving HAIC-based triple therapy.
